title: Ticket Brief
description: Structured extraction from a Jira ticket, PRD, or feature request, produced before generation starts. Keeps 'what does the ticket actually ask for' explicit and separate from the agent's interpretation, so requireTicketPriorityTraceability (composition-heuristics) has something concrete to check against.

ref.description: existing-design: its design-index ID. new-brief: the new brief's title. out-of-scope: the reason. question: the question.

sourceType.description: Where this brief came from. 'page-brief' = written from templates/page-brief.md. A PRD often spans several designs, so it is the most common source of scope overlap — see the scope placement check.

sourceRef.description: Link or path to the source ticket/PRD.

scopeTerms.description: Normalized domain terms this brief is about (lowercase, singular, specific — e.g. 'date-range filter', not 'filter'). Compared against design-index projects' scopeTerms in the scope placement check.

surfaces.description: Screens/areas of the product this brief would change, e.g. ['reports', 'reports/toolbar']. Use the same surface names as the design index.

scopeOverlapReportRef.description: ID of the scope-overlap-report produced for this brief, once the scope placement check has run.

rawDescription.description: Verbatim (paraphrased per copyright practice if fetched from Jira text) ticket description, kept for traceability.

priorities.description: The core things this design must accomplish, ranked. Every major generation decision must cite one of these.

source.description: 'explicit' = stated directly in the ticket. 'acceptance-criterion' = derived from a listed AC. 'inferred' = the agent's read on unstated intent — flagged separately so it can be confirmed rather than assumed.

requiredElements.description: Concrete UI needs pulled from the ticket, each destined for the reuse/similarity check against the manifest's components[].

description.description: e.g. 'a way to show 4 KPIs with trend indicators'.

linkedPriority.description: id of the priority this element serves, for traceability.

states.description: States this element must show, from the brief's States section.

estimatedVolume.description: If this is a list/collection, rough expected item count — feeds compositionHeuristics.listPaginationThreshold check, e.g. '~30 rows, grows over time'.

infoType.description: What kind of information this is. It decides the form it's shown in (tools/purpose_check.py, reference/content-forms.md).

form.description: How it's shown. purpose_check flags a form that doesn't fit the infoType and suggests the forms that do.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Testable statements the design must meet, from the brief (optimized by skills/design-agent/reference/brief-optimization.md). Each is checked against the design output in the audit (rubric category 9).

statement.description: Subject, action and measurable result, e.g. 'An admin can turn off email for one event type in 2 taps or fewer, at 320px.'

source.description: 'rewritten' = the author's criterion made testable; 'inferred' = added from a design-system requirement and confirmed by the author.

connections.description: Where the page fits in the product, from the page brief's 'Where it fits' section. The starting point for the user flow (Step 2c).

mustLinkHere.description: Existing pages that should link to this one.

entities.description: The things this page shows, acts on or needs, and who handles each part of their life (skills/design-agent/reference/edge-case-sweep.md, Step 1). This is where missing parts of the product surface, like an admin side nobody briefed.

nonEntityTerms.description: Scope terms that aren't things with a life of their own (e.g. 'voting window'), so the edge-case check doesn't ask who creates them.

edgeCases.description: The edge-case sweep's findings (skills/design-agent/reference/edge-case-sweep.md, Step 2), each with a decision.

lens.description: One of the standard lenses (ecosystem, roles, setup, time, concurrency, integrity, scale, failure, ending, communication, privacy, access) or a product lens from briefPolicy.edgeCaseLenses.

action.description: in-scope: which AC, element, state or flow path covers it (by id where there is one). new-brief: the brief's title. out-of-scope / not-applicable: the reason. question: the question.

outOfScope.description: What the page deliberately doesn't do. The design must not include these.

approvedBy.description: Who approved the optimized brief. In lite mode this replaces a separate brief-optimization report.

optimizationReportRef.description: The brief-optimization-report that produced this brief from its source.

coreTasks.description: The tasks users come to this design to do. Each is walked against the 3-3-3 rule (design-principles.md) — understood in 3 seconds, reached in 3 clicks, completed in 3 minutes.

statement.description: What the user is trying to get done, e.g. 'Filter the dashboard to the last 30 days.'

entryPoint.description: Where the user starts — the surface they land on, e.g. 'dashboard (after sign-in)'. Clicks are counted from here.

constraints.description: Explicit constraints from the ticket (platform, deadline-driven scope cuts, must-integrate-with-X, etc.).

linkedDesigns.description: URLs/references to existing designs mentioned in the ticket (Figma links, prior screens) that this should be visually consistent with.

openQuestions.description: Ambiguities the agent couldn't resolve from the ticket alone — surfaced to the human before generation starts rather than silently assumed.

brandGuidelines.description: Brand guidelines this work follows, e.g. ['Atari']. Only when the author asks for them: a mention of the brand isn't a request. Declared work is designed, linted and checked against that brand's reference design system (the manifest's brandGuidelines designSystem) instead of the project's.

purpose.description: One sentence: what's true once the user leaves this page (from the page brief's Purpose). tools/purpose_check.py checks that everything on the page serves it.

pageJustification.description: Why this is a page and not a section, panel, tooltip or notification: people come back to it on its own, other pages link to it, or it's too big to fit where it's reached from. Needed when the page has no core task, or is small and reached from one place.

pagePattern.description: The kind of page this is. tools/pattern_check.py suggests it from the brief's words, and lists what that kind of page implies (skills/design-agent/reference/page-patterns.md).

patternDecisions.description: A decision for each capability the page pattern implies, e.g. {ownership: in-scope, reorder: in-scope, after-responses: question}. Questions go to the author at the brief's one stop.
